(p-260) Surah 65: Al-Talaq, Medinan, and its verses are twelve.

﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women﴾: The singling out of the address to him (ﷺ), together with the general application of the address to his community as well, is to honour him (ﷺ), to show the greatness of his station, and to establish that he is the one addressed in reality; the community's inclusion in the address comes by way of his (ﷺ) being addressed and their being subordinate to him, and by giving him precedence over them, not because his address is like their address. For if that consideration were within the sphere of careful regard, the address would be more deserving of it, since its ruling applies to all of them with certainty. The meaning: when you intend to divorce them and have resolved upon it, as in His saying: ﴿When you rise to the prayer﴾.

﴿then divorce them for their waiting period﴾: that is, at the beginning of it, like your saying: "I came to him on the night that had passed of such-and-such a month." For when a woman is divorced in a state of purity that is followed by her first menstrual cycle (qur') of her period, she has been divorced at the beginning of her waiting period. The intended meaning is that they should be divorced in a purity during which no intercourse has taken place, and then left alone until their waiting period is completed. This is the best form of divorce and the most fitting of it in accordance with the Sunnah.

﴿and count the waiting period﴾: keep exact account of it and complete it as three full menstrual cycles (quru').

﴿and fear God, your Lord﴾: regarding prolonging the waiting period for them and harming them. Describing Him, exalted is He, with His lordship over them is an emphasis on the command and an intensification in making God-consciousness (taqwa) obligatory.

﴿Do not expel them from their houses﴾: from their dwellings at the time of separation until their waiting period is completed. Attributing the houses to them, though they belong to their husbands, is to emphasise the prohibition by showing how fully they deserve to dwell in them, as if the houses were their own property.

﴿nor let them leave﴾: even with your permission, for permission to leave carries the same ruling as expulsion. It has also been said that the meaning is: they should not leave by their own independent decision; but if both agree to leave, it is permissible, since the right belongs to neither of them alone.

﴿unless they commit a clear immorality﴾: this is an exception from the first clause. It has been said that it is adultery, so that they may leave in order to have the prescribed punishment carried out upon them. It has also been said: unless they act ill-manneredly (yabdhūna) toward their husbands, in which case their removal becomes lawful at that point. This is supported by the reading "unless they act viciously toward you" (yufhishna ʿalaykum). Or it is an exception from the second clause, for the sake of intensifying the prohibition on leaving, by stating that their leaving is an immorality.

﴿These﴾ is a pointer to the rulings mentioned. The "mā" in the demonstrative carries a sense of distance, despite the nearness of what is pointed to, to signal the exalted rank of these rulings and the remoteness of their station.

﴿are the limits of God﴾: which He has set for His servants.

﴿And whoever transgresses the limits of God﴾: that is, His limits mentioned above, by neglecting any part of them. The explicit mention here in place of a pronoun serves to magnify the matter of transgression and to indicate the reason for the ruling in His saying:

﴿then he has wronged himself﴾: that is, he has harmed himself. Interpreting wronging as exposing oneself to punishment is ruled out by (p-261) His saying: ﴿You do not know; perhaps God will bring about after that some matter﴾. For this is a resumptive clause brought to explain the content of the conditional sentence. They have said that the matter God brings about is that He turns his heart away from what he did in transgression to its opposite. So the wronging must be an expression for a worldly harm that befalls him because of his transgression and cannot be remedied, or for harm in general, encompassing both worldly and otherworldly harm. The explanation is restricted to the worldly, because people's caution against it is greater and their concern to avert it is more intense. His saying: ﴿You do not know﴾ is an address to the transgressor by way of iltifat (shift of grammatical person), for greater emphasis in warning against transgression, not to the Prophet (ﷺ) as has been imagined. The meaning: whoever transgresses the limits of God has harmed himself; for you, O transgressor, do not know the outcome of the matter. Perhaps God will bring about in your heart, after what you have done of transgression, a matter that requires the opposite of what you did, so that hatred is changed into love, and turning away into turning toward her; and it becomes possible to remedy it by reconciliation (raj'a) or by beginning a new marriage contract.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 65, verse 2:

﴿When they have reached their term﴾ means they have come close to the end of their 'iddah (waiting period).

﴿Then retain them﴾ means take them back (ruju').

﴿in a fair manner﴾ means with good companionship and suitable maintenance.

﴿or part from them in a fair manner﴾ means by fulfilling their right and avoiding harm, such as when he takes her back and then divorces her in order to prolong the 'iddah.

﴿And call to witness two just men from among you﴾ at the time of the return (ruju') or the separation, to cut off dispute. This is a command of recommendation (amr nadb), as in the words of His Exalted Name: ﴿And call to witness when you trade﴾. It is narrated from al-Shafi'i (Shafi'i, the jurist) that it is obligatory at the time of return.

﴿And establish the testimony for God﴾ O witnesses, when it is needed, sincerely for His Exalted Face.

﴿That﴾ is a reference to the exhortation to call witnesses and to establish testimony, or to everything mentioned in the verse.

﴿With it is admonished whoever among you believes in God and the Last Day﴾ for he is the one who benefits from it, and the intent is to remind him. His Exalted Name's words ﴿And whoever fears God...﴾ etc. form a parenthetical clause (jumla i'tiradiyya) confirming what preceded about the obligation to observe God's limits, by promising reward for guarding against transgressing them, just as His Exalted Name's earlier words ﴿And whoever transgresses the limits of God has certainly wronged himself﴾ confirm it by threatening those who transgress them. The meaning is: whoever fears God, divorces according to the Sunnah, does not harm the woman in her 'iddah, does not evict her from her dwelling, and takes precaution regarding witnessing and other matters.

﴿He will make for him a way out﴾ from the distresses and tight situations that may befall matters of spouses, and He will relieve him of the anxieties that afflict him.

**Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 65, verse 3:**

﴿وَيَرْزُقْهُ مِن حَيْثُ لا يَحْتَسِبُ﴾ That is: from a source that does not occur to him and that he does not expect. It is also possible that this is a statement brought in by way of digression (istitrad) when mentioning His words, exalted is He: ﴿That is what you are admonished with, whoever believes in God...﴾ to the end of the verse. The meaning is: whoever fears God in everything he does and everything he omits, He will make for him a way out and a deliverance from the troubles of this world and the Hereafter. Thus what we are discussing falls within it as a primary inclusion.

"From the Prophet, peace be upon him, that he recited it and said: 'A way out from the doubts of this world, from the agonies of death, and from the hardships of the Day of Resurrection.'" And the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: ﴿Indeed I know a verse which, if people took hold of it, would suffice them: And whoever fears God...﴾ So he kept reciting it and repeating it. It is also narrated that "the polytheists captured his son Salim, so Awf ibn al-Ashja'i came to the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, and said: 'My son has been taken captive,' and he complained to him of poverty. The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: 'Fear God and repeat often: There is no power and no strength except through God, the Most High, the Mighty.' He did so, and while he was in his house, his son knocked on the door, and with him were a hundred camels which the enemy had neglected, and he had driven them off. So this verse was revealed." ﴿And whoever relies upon God, He is sufficient for him﴾ That is: He is sufficient for him in all his affairs.

﴿Indeed God accomplishes His command﴾ With the genitive construction (bi-l-idafa), that is: He carries out His command. It is read with tanwin on bali<u>gh</u> and the accusative on "amrihi," that is: He reaches what He wills; no desired thing escapes Him and no sought thing overcomes Him. It is also read with the nominative on "amrihi," in which case "bali<u>gh</u>" is a predicate preceding its subject and the clause is the predicate of "inna," or "bali<u>gh</u>" is the predicate of "inna" and "amruhu" is raised by it as its agent, that is: His command is executed. It is also read "bali<u>gh</u>an amrahu," in which case it is a circumstantial clause (hal), and the predicate of "inna" is His words, exalted is He: ﴿God has set a measure for everything﴾ That is: a determination and a fixed time, or a quantity. This is an explanation of the obligation to rely upon Him, exalted is He, and to entrust the matter to Him, because when a person knows that everything, including provision and other things, happens only by His determination, exalted is He, nothing remains except submission to the decree and reliance upon God, exalted is He.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 65, verse 4:

﴿And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation﴾ because of their old age. They have estimated this as sixty years, and as fifty-five.

﴿If you are in doubt﴾, i.e., you are uncertain and do not know what their 'iddah (waiting period) is.

﴿Then their 'iddah is three months, and those who have not yet menstruated﴾ due to their youth, i.e., their 'iddah is likewise so. The verb has been elided, relying on the indication of what precedes it.

﴿And for those who are pregnant, their term is﴾, i.e., the end of their 'iddah.

﴿That they lay down their burden﴾, whether they are divorced or widowed. The generality of His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿Those of you who die and leave wives behind, they shall wait by themselves four months and ten days﴾, has been abrogated by this, since its revelation came later than that. This accords with the well-known statement of Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him: "Whoever wishes, I will invoke a curse upon him: the shorter Surat al-Nisa' was revealed after the one in Surat al-Baqarah." It is also authentically related that "Subay'ah bint al-Harith al-Aslamiyyah gave birth a few nights after her husband's death, and she mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said to her: 'You have been released, so marry.'" ﴿And whoever fears Allah﴾ in regard to His rulings and observing their rights.

﴿He will make for him of his affair ease﴾, i.e., He will facilitate his affair for him and grant him success in goodness.

"That" refers to the rulings mentioned, and the sense of distance in it, despite the recency of what is referred to, serves to announce the高 elevation of its rank in excellence. The particle *al-kaf* (the second-person suffix) is used in the singular, although the address is plural, as His saying makes clear: ﴿The command of God, He has sent it down to you﴾. This is because it serves merely to distinguish the present from the past, not to specify the particular identity of those addressed. This was discussed in His saying, ﴿That is admonished thereby whoever among you believes in God﴾, in Surat al-Baqarah.

﴿And whoever fears God﴾ by guarding His rulings.

﴿He will remove from him his misdeeds﴾, for good deeds remove misdeeds.

﴿And will magnify for him a reward﴾ by multiplication.

(p-263) And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Lodge them where you dwell, according to your means, and do not harm them so as to constrict them. And if they are pregnant, spend on them until they give birth. Then if they nurse for you, give them their payment, and confer among yourselves in kindness. But if you disagree, then another woman will nurse for him﴾.

﴿Lodge them where you dwell﴾ is a resumptive clause (isti'naf) that comes as an answer to a question arising from what precedes it, namely the exhortation to taqwa (God-consciousness). It is as if it were said: "How do we act upon taqwa concerning the women in waiting (mu'taddat)?" So it was said: "Lodge them in a dwelling from where you dwell," i.e., in some part of your dwelling place. His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿according to your means﴾, i.e., according to your capacity, meaning that which you are able to afford, is an explicative apposition (ʿatf bayan) to His saying "from where you dwell" and an elaboration of it.

﴿And do not harm them﴾, i.e., regarding the lodging.

﴿so as to constrict them﴾, and force them to leave.

﴿And if they are﴾, i.e., the divorced women,

﴿pregnant, spend on them until they give birth﴾, whereupon they come out of the waiting period (iddah). As for women whose husbands have died, there is no maintenance (nafaqah) for them.

﴿Then if they nurse for you﴾ after that.

﴿then give them their payment﴾ for the nursing.

﴿and confer among yourselves in kindness﴾, i.e., consult one another. Its real meaning is that some of you should command one another to what is good regarding nursing and payment, and there should be neither obstinacy (mumasakah) on the part of the father nor hardship (mu'asarah) on the part of the mother.

﴿But if you disagree﴾, i.e., you become constricted.

﴿then another woman will nurse for him﴾, i.e., another nursing woman will be found and none will be lacking; and in this there is a rebuke to the mother for her obstinacy.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 65, verse 7:

﴿Let the one of wide means spend from his wide means, and whoever has his provision restricted, let him spend from what Allah has given him.﴾ And even if it is little. That is: let each one of the wealthy and the poor spend what his capacity reaches.

﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond what He has given it.﴾ (Allah, exalted is He, whether much or little, does not burden any soul except according to its capacity.) In this there is consolation for the heart of the poor person and encouragement for him to give what he can, and this is reinforced by the promise where it is said: ﴿Allah will bring about ease after hardship.﴾ That is: sooner or later.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 65, verse 8:

﴿And how many a town﴾ means: many of the people of a town.

﴿Rebelled﴾ means: turned away.

﴿from the command of its Lord and His messengers﴾ with arrogance, defiance and obstinacy.

﴿So We called it to a severe reckoning﴾ with thorough investigation, scrutiny and close examination of every speck and every trifle.

﴿And We punished it with a dreadful punishment﴾ meaning: a great and terrible punishment. It has also been read as "nukran" (nukran). What is intended is the reckoning of the Hereafter and its punishment, and the expression of them in the past tense serves to indicate their certainty, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the companions of the Garden will call out﴾.
﴿So she tasted the evil consequence of her affair, and the outcome of her affair was ruin﴾, a terrible loss beyond which there is no further loss.

﴿Allah has prepared for them a severe punishment.﴾ This repeats the threat and clarifies that it is awaited, as if it were said: "Allah has prepared this punishment for them."

﴿So fear Allah, O people of understanding, who believe.﴾ It is permissible that "the reckoning" refers to the thorough recording of their sins and their inscription in the records of the recording angels (al-Hafazah), and that "the punishment" refers to what befell them in this world. It has also been permitted that ﴿they tasted the evil consequence of their affair﴾ [the phrase "ʿataat" and what is conjoined to it] be an attributive qualifier of "the town," and that ﴿Allah has prepared for them﴾ be the response to His words, exalted is He, ﴿How many a town﴾ [wa-ka-ayyin].

﴿Who believe﴾ is in the accusative case by an implied verb of the form أعْنِي (a'ni, "I mean"), as an explanatory clarification of the addressed party (al-munada, the vocative). Or it is an explicative apposition (ʿatf bayan) to it, or a descriptive adjective (naʿt). Its substitution (ibdal) for the vocative is weak, because it cannot occupy the latter's position.

﴿Allah has sent down to you a reminder﴾ refers to Jibril (peace be upon him). He was named thus because of the frequency of his remembrance (of Allah), or because he descended with the reminder, which is the Qur'an, as is indicated by the substitution (ibdal) of the words of His exalted saying:

﴿A messenger﴾ from Him, or because he is mentioned (مَذْكُورٌ) in the heavens and among the nations. Or "dhikr" (الذِّكْرِ) is meant in the sense of honour (الشَّرَفُ), as in His saying: ﴿And indeed it is a reminder for you and for your people﴾. It is as if it is in itself an honour, either because it is an honour for the one to whom it was sent down, or because it is endowed with glory and honour with Allah, Exalted, as in His saying: ﴿with the Lord of the Throne, secure in position﴾.

Or it refers to the Prophet, upon him be prayers and peace, and this is the view of most scholars. He is referred to as "dhikr" because of his constancy in reciting the Qur'an, or in conveying it and reminding people of it. His sending (إرْسالِهِ) is expressed by "sending down" (الإنْزالِ) as a figurative device (بِطَرِيقِ التَّرْشِيحِ, a rhetorical method of developing a metaphor). Or it is because his sending is caused by the sending down of the revelation to him. "Rasūlan" (رَسُولًا) is substituted from it (أُبْدِلَ مِنهُ) as an explanatory apposition (لِلْبَيانِ). Or "dhikr" is the Qur'an, and "rasūlan" (رَسُولًا) is governed by an implied verb like "arsala" (أرْسَلَ, "he sent"), or it is governed by "dhikran" (ذِكْرًا) through the grammatical principle of making the verbal noun with tanwin (إعْمالِ المَصْدَرِ المُنَوَّنِ) act, or it is a substitution from it on the basis that it carries the meaning of "risālah" (الرِّسالَةِ, "message").

His saying: ﴿who recites to you the clear signs of Allah﴾ is a qualifier (نَعْتٌ) of "rasūlan" (رَسُولًا). "Āyāt Allāh" (آياتِ اللَّهِ) means the Qur'an, and "bayyināt" (بَيِّناتٍ) is a circumstantial qualifier (حالٌ) of it, meaning: while they are making clear to you what you need of the rulings. It is also read as "mubayyanāt" (مُبَيَّناتٍ), meaning that Allah has made them clear, in accordance with His saying: ﴿We have already made the signs clear for you﴾.

The lām (اللّامُ) in His saying: ﴿so that He may bring out those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ is connected to "yatlū" (يَتْلُو) or to "anzala" (أنْزَلَ). On the first view, the subject of "yakhruju" (يَخْرُجُ) is the pronoun of the Messenger, upon him be prayers and peace, or the pronoun referring to Allah, and the relative pronoun refers to the believers after the sending down, meaning: so that there may be attained for them, by the Messenger or by Allah, Exalted and Majestic, what they are now upon of faith and righteous deeds. Or it means: so that He may bring out those whom He knows or foreordains will believe.

﴿From the darkness into the light﴾: from misguidance into guidance.

﴿And whoever believes in Allah and does righteousness﴾: as has been made clear within the clear verses that were sent down.

﴿He will admit him into gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾. It is also read as "nudkhiluhu" (نُدْخِلْهُ) with the letter nūn. His saying: ﴿abiding therein forever﴾ is a circumstantial qualifier (حالٌ) of the object of "yudkhilhu" (يُدْخِلْهُ), and the plural form is in accordance with the meaning of "man" (مَن), just as the singular form in the three pronouns is in accordance with its wording. His saying: ﴿Allah has certainly made good provision for him﴾ is another circumstantial qualifier of him, or of the pronoun in "khālidīna" (خالِدِينَ), through the method of interlocking (بِطَرِيقِ التَّداخُلِ). The singular form of the pronoun in "lahu" (لَهُ) has already been explained. It carries the meaning of wonder and exalting what Allah has granted the believers in reward.

﴿Allah is He who created seven heavens﴾ is a mubtada' (subject) and khabar (predicate) construction.

﴿And of the earth, the like of them﴾: that is, He created from the earth the like of them in number. It is recited as "mithluhunna" with a nominative vowel, meaning that it is a mubtada' (subject) and "min al-ardi" (of the earth) is its khabar (predicate). Scholars differ over the manner of the layers of the earth. The majority hold that they are seven earths, layered one above another, with a distance between each earth and the next, just as there is a distance between the heaven and the earth, and that each earth has inhabitants from among the creatures of Allah, exalted is He. Al-Dahhak said: they are layered closely upon one another without gaps, unlike the heavens. Al-Qurtubi said: the first view is more sound, because the reports indicate it, as al-Bukhari and others narrated that Ka'b swore by He who split the sea for Musa that Suhayb had told him that the Prophet (ﷺ) did not see a town he wished to enter without saying when he saw it: "O Allah, Lord of the seven heavens and what they shade, Lord of the seven earths and what they carry, Lord of the devils and those they lead astray, Lord of the winds and what they scatter, we ask You for the good of this town and the good of its people, and we seek refuge in You from its evil, the evil of its people, and the evil of what is in it."

It is also narrated on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that Nafi' ibn al-Azraq asked him whether there were creatures beneath the earths. He said: Yes. He asked: What are the creatures? He said: Either angels or jinn. Al-Mawardi said: On this view, the call of Islam is restricted to the inhabitants of the upper earth, excluding others, even if there are rational creatures in the lower earths. As for whether they see the sky and draw light from it, there are two views. One is that they see the sky from every side of their earth and draw light from it. The other is that they do not see the sky, and that Allah created for them a light which they see. Al-Kalbi related from Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that they are seven earths scattered among seas, and the sky shades them all.

﴿The command descends among them﴾: that is, His command and decree proceed among them and His dominion takes effect within them. It is narrated from Qatadah: in every heaven and in every earth there is a creation of His, a command of His, and a decree of His. It was also said: it is what is administered within them of the wonders of His management. It is recited as "yanzilu al-amr" (the command descends).

﴿That you may know that Allah is over all things competent﴾: this is connected to "created" or to "descends," or to an implied verb that covers both. That is: He did that so that you may know that whoever is able to do what has been mentioned is able to do all things.

﴿And that Allah has encompassed all things in knowledge﴾: because it is impossible for the mentioned acts to proceed from one who is not like this. It is also permissible that the verb governing the lam (in "li-ta'lamu") be an explanation of the creation mentioned and the descent of the command, meaning: He revealed that and made it clear, so that you may know, through what He mentioned of the matters you witness and those you receive through revelation, of the wonders of created things, that nothing whatsoever goes beyond His power and knowledge. It is also recited as "liya'lamu" (that they may know).

It is narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever recites Surah al-Talaq dies upon the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."
